items.problem: `release` "cleans up the same way as `detach_camera`", which ends a `move_to`/`zoom_to` in progress with `Cancelled` (line 70). skills/core/SKILL.md:70 says `release` stops the async operations in progress and "a stopped operation returns a failure value", and the failure value of `move_to`, `move_by_preset` and `zoom_to` is `Failed` (camera-core.md:33-37). The two documents give different results for `release` during a `move_to`

It is not set whether bounds fitting writes the fitted value back into the base position or only produces the value of step 2 (`get_view_center` is "base position after bounds fitting", line 44; line 108 says a 3D camera "moves" the base position's horizontal axes). Run path: `snap_to`(p outside the bounds) → `set_bounds` → frame → `clear_bounds` → frame. The camera either stays at the fitted position or returns to p. This also affects row 146, "the base position keeps its value at the call", when `set_bounds` or `zoom_to` runs while a `move_by_preset` waits for loading

The failure conditions of `follow` (lines 31, 87, 144) cover a missing or destroyed target, negative smooth time and negative dead zone size, but not a target object that has no world position of the attached camera's dimension (e.g. in Godot a `Node2D` target for a `Camera3D`, or a plain `Node`). "target object position" (line 87) is then not defined, so one implementation can fail with `false`, another can project or pad the axes. `CutsceneCore` checks the dimension itself before calling `CameraCore` (skills/client-core/modules/cutscene-core.md:75), which shows `CameraCore` does not define it. This existed before the diff and is unrelated to the changed side effect on the `move_to` in progress
